long.vo: In the T20 series in New Zealand, India's batters went after almost everyone. New Zealand's seamers went for nearly eleven an over. But one bowler, New Zealand's own captain, India simply couldn't hit.
Look at the economy rates. New Zealand's seamers, ten point six five an over. Michael Bracewell's off-spin, over twelve. Mitchell Santner? Seven point three seven.
Across the series, Santner bowled nineteen overs and took nine wickets, including four for twenty-one in the second match. No other New Zealand bowler came close.

And this wasn't a timid Indian batting line-up. Against pace, अभिषेक शर्मा struck at two hundred and fifty-six. Naman Dhir, over two hundred. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, one eighty-five. As a team, India scored at one seventy-eight against the seamers.

Now compare that with Santner. Against the seamers, India scored at one seventy-eight and lost a wicket every seventeen balls. Against Santner, they scored at just one twenty-three, and lost a wicket every thirteen balls.

So who struggled most? तिलक वर्मा made just nineteen off twenty-one balls against him. श्रेयस अय्यर scored at a run a ball and fell to him twice. Sanju Samson struck at one-fourteen. Only Naman Dhir really took him on.

head.sub: STRIKE RATE · BALLS FACED IN BRACKETS

long.vo: Why did it work? First, he owned the middle overs: almost all his deliveries came between overs seven and fifteen, when India wanted to accelerate. Second, it didn't matter which hand you batted with. Left-handers struck at one sixteen against him, right-handers at one twenty-eight. And third, this wasn't about spin in general. Bracewell's off-spin went for twelve an over.

items.d: 108 of his 114 balls came in overs 7–15
Bracewell's off-spin went at 12.17 an over

long.vo: Game by game, he was a constant threat: two for thirty-nine, then four for twenty-one, one for seventeen, and two for twenty-four. Only in the final match did India finally get after him, nought for thirty-nine. But by then, New Zealand had found their rhythm and won the last two games.

Our verdict? India won the series three-two. But Santner won his battle. And with the next T20 World Cup cycle starting, left-arm spin in the middle overs is the weakness every opponent will now target.
